# Illustrating the `httr2` functions

```{r slide08}
httr2::request("https://data.cincinnati-oh.gov/resource/rvmt-pkmq.json") |>
  httr2::req_url_query("$limit" = 5) |>
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_string() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON()
```


## FRED Example

```{r fred}
library(httr2)
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

# 1. Fetch data from FRED API
ohio_jobs <- request("https://api.stlouisfed.org/fred/series/observations") |>
  req_url_query(
    series_id = "IHLIDXUSOH",
    api_key = Sys.getenv("FRED_API_KEY"), # Ensure key is active
    file_type = "json"
  ) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_string() |>
  fromJSON()

# 2. Extract observations dataframe
ohio_df <- ohio_jobs$observations

# 3. Mutate date column and filter using Date object
ohio_df_sept_2026 <- ohio_df |> 
  mutate(
    date = ymd(date),
    value = as.numeric(value) # Also parse character values into numeric
  ) |> 
  filter(date >= ymd("2026-09-01"))

glimpse(ohio_df_sept_2026)
```


## USA Jobs

```{r usajobs}
httr2::request("https://data.usajobs.gov/api/search") |>
  httr2::req_url_query(Keyword = "Data Analyst", ResultsPerPage = 500) |>
  httr2::req_headers(
    Host = "data.usajobs.gov",
    "User-Agent" = "fmegahed@miamioh.edu",
    "Authorization-Key" = Sys.getenv("USAJOBS_API_KEY")
  ) |>
  httr2::req_perform() |> 
  httr2::resp_body_string() |> 
  jsonlite::fromJSON(flatten = T) -> usa_jobs_data


usa_jobs_df = usa_jobs_data$SearchResult$SearchResultItems

jobs_small = usa_jobs_df |>
  dplyr::select(
    title = MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle,
    department = MatchedObjectDescriptor.DepartmentName,
    agency = MatchedObjectDescriptor.OrganizationName,
    location = MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionLocationDisplay,
    closes = MatchedObjectDescriptor.ApplicationCloseDate
  )

## Easy way -- since we looked for data analyst as a key word
nrow(jobs_small)
# q 2
table(jobs_small$department) |> sort(decreasing = T) |> head(3)
jobs_small |> dplyr::count(department) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n)) |> head(3)

## The harder way (but being literal)
jobs_small |> dplyr::filter(title == 'Data Analyst') -> count_literal

count_literal |> dplyr::count(department) |> dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n))

## the harder way (without being literal)
# Jesse -> Data Analyst or Data Analytics side-by-side
index_data_analyst = jobs_small$title |> 
  stringr::str_detect("Data Analytics|Data Analyst")

# given that this is a true or fale type result
# true rows will be kept
# , nothing means keep all columns
count_jesse_standard = jobs_small[index_data_analyst , ]
count_jesse_standard  |> dplyr::count(department) |> dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n))
```
